gloss: to let escape; to miss; to lose

definitions.gloss: to let escape; to set free
definitions.explanation: To allow someone or something to get away.
To fail to take advantage of an opportunity or chance.

examples.english: I let the fish get away.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}を{逃|のが}してしまった。
{捕|つか}まえた{鳥|とり}を{逃|のが}してしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally let the bird I caught escape.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{手|て}を{離|はな}したので、{犬|いぬ}を{逃|のが}してしまった。
examples.english: The child let go of the leash, so we let the dog get away.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{長|なが}い{間|あいだ}{追|お}いかけていた{犯人|はんにん}をまた{逃|のが}してしまった。
examples.english: The police let the criminal they had been chasing for a long time escape again.

examples.japanese: このチャンスを{逃|のが}したくない。
examples.english: I don't want to miss this chance.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}を{逃|のが}して{遅刻|ちこく}した。
examples.english: I missed the train and was late.

examples.japanese: せっかくの{機会|きかい}を{逃|のが}してしまった。
examples.english: I let a great opportunity slip away.

examples.japanese: {安|やす}く{買|か}えるチャンスを{逃|のが}して、とても{残念|ざんねん}だった。
examples.english: I missed the chance to buy it cheaply and was very disappointed.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}のバスを{逃|のが}してしまったので、{歩|ある}いて{家|いえ}まで{帰|かえ}らなければならなかった。
examples.english: I missed the last bus, so I had to walk home.

notes:
{逃|のが}す is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}). The intransitive pair is {逃|のが}れる (to escape).

ASPECT ({ている}):
{逃|のが}している is rarely used; the past tense {逃|のが}した (missed/let escape) is more common.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- チャンスを{逃|のが}す - to miss a chance
- {機会|きかい}を{逃|のが}す - to miss an opportunity
- {電車|でんしゃ}を{逃|のが}す - to miss a train
- {犯人|はんにん}を{逃|のが}す - to let a criminal escape
- {見|み}{逃|のが}す - to overlook, to miss seeing

{逃|のが}す VS {逃|に}がす:
Both readings exist with the same meaning, but {逃|のが}す is more common in standard speech. {逃|に}がす may be heard in some dialects.

COMPOUND VERBS:
- {見逃|みのが}す - to overlook, to let pass
- {聞|き}き{逃|のが}す - to miss hearing
